blocks.body: As a service provider, we are responsible for our own content on these pages under general law (§ 7 (1) DDG). We are not, however, obliged to monitor third-party information we transmit or store, nor to actively investigate circumstances indicating unlawful activity (§§ 8 to 10 DDG). Obligations to remove or block the use of information under general law remain unaffected; any such liability arises only from the point at which we become aware of a specific infringement. As soon as we do, we will remove the content concerned without delay.

This site contains links to external sites over whose content we have no influence. We therefore cannot accept any warranty for that third-party content: the provider or operator of those pages is always solely responsible for it. Those sites were checked at the time of linking and no unlawful content was discernible then. Permanent monitoring is not reasonable without concrete evidence of an infringement; as soon as we become aware of one, we will remove the link without delay.

Unless otherwise stated, content and works created by the association on this site are published under a Creative Commons CC BY-SA 4.0 licence. You may therefore reproduce, adapt and distribute them, including commercially, on two conditions: credit Ayiti Dijital, and share any derivative under the same licence.

Content not created by the association remains subject to the rights of its authors and is marked as such; this applies in particular to third-party trademarks, logos and photographs, which the licence above does not cover. Should you nonetheless notice an infringement of copyright, please tell us: as soon as we become aware of one, we will remove the content concerned without delay.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.subtitle: within the meaning of Art. 4 GDPR

blocks.body: This page uses the regulation's vocabulary. Here is what those terms mean, in the sense given by Art. 4 GDPR.

items.title: Personal data
items.body: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person, directly or indirectly: a name, a number, location data, an online identifier (Art. 4(1)).

items.title: Data subject
items.body: The identified or identifiable natural person whose data is processed — in this case, you.

items.title: Processing
items.body: Any operation performed on data: collection, recording, organisation, storage, consultation, disclosure, erasure, destruction (Art. 4(2)).

items.title: Restriction of processing
items.body: Marking stored data so as to limit its future processing (Art. 4(3)).

items.title: Profiling
items.body: Automated processing to evaluate or predict personal aspects — behaviour, interests, economic situation, movements (Art. 4(4)).

items.title: Pseudonymisation
items.body: Processing such that data can no longer be attributed to a person without additional information, kept separately (Art. 4(5)).

items.title: Controller
items.body: Whoever determines the purposes and means of processing (Art. 4(7)). For this site, the association.

items.title: Processor
items.body: A third party processing data on the controller's behalf and on its instructions (Art. 4(8)) — here, our host.

items.title: Recipient
items.body: Any body to which data is disclosed, whether a third party or not; authorities acting under a specific inquiry are not recipients (Art. 4(9)).

items.title: Third party
items.body: Any body other than the data subject, the controller, the processor, and persons authorised to process the data under their authority (Art. 4(10)).

items.title: Consent
items.body: A freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication that you agree to a processing operation (Art. 4(11)).

blocks.body: These are the regulation's own definitions, restated here for clarity; they describe the vocabulary, not our practices. We carry out neither profiling nor pseudonymisation.
Processing personal data is lawful only where it rests on one of the grounds in Art. 6 GDPR.

items.title: Consent — Art. 6(1)(a)
items.body: You explicitly agree to a particular processing operation, and may withdraw that agreement at any time.

items.title: Contract — Art. 6(1)(b)
items.body: The processing is necessary to perform a contract or to take pre-contractual steps.

items.title: Legal obligation — Art. 6(1)(c)
items.body: The law requires us to process or retain certain data, for instance for accounting.

items.title: Legitimate interest — Art. 6(1)(f)
items.body: The processing is necessary to run the site securely and your rights and freedoms do not override it.

blocks.body: Today only legitimate interest applies to this site, and only for the technical data required to deliver the pages. We ask for no consent, because we do nothing that requires one.

sections.title: Hosting, server logs and transfers outside the EU

blocks.body: This site is hosted by Vercel Inc. (United States), acting as our processor. To deliver a page, your browser necessarily transmits technical data to the host: your IP address, the date and time of the request, the address requested, the referring site and your browser type. That data serves to deliver the site, keep it secure and diagnose faults. It is not used to identify you and is not combined with any other information.

This processing is essential to making the site available and rests on our legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). As Vercel is a US company, a transfer of this technical data to a third country within the meaning of Art. 44 ff. GDPR cannot be excluded.

This site is served over HTTPS only: everything exchanged between your browser and the server is encrypted using TLS. You can tell by the address, which begins with “https://”. That encryption stops third parties reading what you look at in transit, and forms part of the technical measures required by Art. 25 and Art. 32 GDPR.
This site sets no cookies and writes nothing to your browser's local storage. That is why you will not see a consent banner: there is nothing to accept or decline.
None. We use neither Google Analytics, nor Plausible, nor any other analytics, tracking or advertising tool. We do not know how many people visit this site.

Fonts are installed on and loaded from our own domain: your browser contacts no Google server. The same goes for images. The site embeds no video, maps, fonts, widgets or scripts from any third-party service.

We maintain profiles on several social networks, and the footer links to them. Those are plain links: no “like” button, no thumbnail and no script from those platforms is embedded in this site. Your browser does not contact them, and they learn nothing about your visit unless you click.
The moment you follow such a link you leave this site: the terms and privacy policy of that platform then apply, and we have no influence over the data it collects.

The newsletter forms on this site are not yet connected to a delivery service: anything entered is neither transmitted nor stored. Once those forms go live, this page will be updated before any data is collected.

We retain no personal data from this site, because we collect none. The technical data needed to deliver the pages is processed by our host and kept for a limited period, for security and diagnostics.
Were we to collect data — through a working form, say — we would keep it only as long as the purpose requires, or as long as a legal obligation demands, and then erase it.
The GDPR grants you the following rights over your personal data.

items.title: Right of access
items.body: Obtain confirmation that data about you is processed, and a copy of it.

items.title: Right to rectification
items.body: Correct any inaccurate or incomplete data.

items.title: Right to erasure
items.body: Request deletion of your data, unless a legal obligation requires otherwise.

items.title: Right to restriction
items.body: Restrict the processing of your data in certain cases.

items.title: Right to portability
items.body: Receive your data in a structured, reusable format.

items.title: Right to object
items.body: Object at any time to processing based on our legitimate interest.

items.title: Withdrawal of consent
items.body: Withdraw a consent at any time, without affecting the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal.

items.title: Automated decisions
items.body: Not be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing. We make none.

blocks.body: To exercise these rights, write to kontakt@ayitidijital.org; we respond within 30 days. Exercising them is free of charge.
Independently of any recourse to us, you may lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. Ours is:
Bavaria splits supervision between two bodies: the BayLfD oversees public bodies, the BayLDA private ones — associations included.
For any question about the protection of your data, exercising your rights, a complaint or a request, write to us directly.

intro: Should you one day wish to use a particular service of the association — writing to us, joining, subscribing to the newsletter — processing your data could become necessary. Where such processing is necessary and no legal basis covers it, we obtain your consent first.

This notice explains which data we process as controller, which data the processors we appoint handle — our host, for instance — and what rights you have. By “personal data” we mean information within the meaning of Art. 4(1) GDPR: a name, an email address, a postal address.
